2.5 Attendance to International Meetings
During our fellowship scheme we attended two international Meetings:

-­‐ The “10th Vaccine Congress” from 4–7 September 2016 in Amsterdam, the

Netherlands. The attendance at this congress is financially supported by WH0 – TDR.
The congress, focused on the vaccine science aim at bringing together the leading
experts in the field of vaccinology to share the latest related information. I attended
two workshops during this congress, one on the scientific publication “Publish or
perish. How to Become a Successful Author” and the other on “How to raise funding
for your research”. The attendance at this congress was an opportunity to get more
familiarized with good practice in vaccinology, to expand my knowledge in vaccine
sciences
-­‐ The 8th EDCTP Forum, from November 6–9, 2016, Lusaka, Zambia. The attend ance
to this Forum was granted by the EDCTP Scholarship. We participated with a poster
communication. The EDCTP Forum is one of the big conference to exchange ideas
between scientist, policy makers and funders about the prevalent diseases in Africa
such as malaria, HIV, tuberculosis, diarrheal diseases and the neglected tropical
diseases. We attended several scientific presentations and workshop such as: Grant
agreement preparation with EDCTP 2 (Organisers: EDCTP and Fit for Health 2.0),
From Research to Publication (Organisers: British Medical Journal (BMJ, United
Kingdom)).

2.6 Planned Activities after the Fellowship Period
The planned activities after the 12 months of the fellowship at IVI are mainly the review and
the development of two manuscripts for publication with my supervisor (Dr. Jean-Louis
Excler) and the Policy and Economic Research Department of IVI.

2.7 Appraisal from the Fellow

This CRD fellowship programme offered me in a good learning environment for clinical
research and also for personal development with a multicultural profile of IVI. It also gave me
the opportunity to meet people who are advanced clinical research scientists. As a beginner,
I tried to benefit of the maximum of inspiring information from them.
The CRD fellowship programme enabled me to expand more my vision, to get clear
professional career goals and to be more confident for the development of trial protocols and
the conduct of clinical trial according to the international standard. I am confident in my
abilities to make significant contribution and to impact positively the conduct of clinical
research activities.
IVI with its knowledge, know-how and skills in clinical research through its core departments
of “Development and Delivery Unit” (Clinical Trial and Regulatory, Biostatistics and Data
Management, Epidemiology, Policy and Health Economics) provided me an appropriate and
a supportive learning environment.
